# GoodAIPromt: full prompt library

A free AI prompt library for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Midjourney and AI video tools. Fill in the blanks, copy the prompt, get better answers. New prompts daily.

Placeholders in [SQUARE BRACKETS] are for the user's own details. Source: https://goodaipromt.com/

## ChatGPT prompts for accountants: tax season emails

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/accountant-tax-season-client-emails/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Write a tax season email series for accounting clients, from document checklist to deadline reminders, in a clear and calm firm voice.

Prompt:

You are an email marketer who works with accounting and tax firms.

Write a tax season email series for [FIRM NAME], an accounting firm serving [CLIENT TYPE, E.G. FAMILIES AND SMALL BUSINESS OWNERS] in [COUNTRY / STATE].

Details:
- How clients send documents: [CLIENT PORTAL / SECURE UPLOAD / DROP-OFF]
- Our internal cut-off for documents: [DATE]
- Official filing deadline we work to: [DATE]
- Extension policy: [HOW EXTENSIONS WORK AT OUR FIRM]
- Fees or changes this year: [NEW FEES, NEW SERVICES OR "NONE"]
- Tone: [WARM AND PLAIN / BRIEF AND FORMAL]

Write 5 emails:
1. Season kickoff: what is new this year and how the process works.
2. Document checklist: a scannable checklist split into "everyone", "if you own a business", "if you own rental property" and "if your life changed this year" (marriage, new child, move, job change).
3. Gentle nudge to clients who have not uploaded anything yet.
4. Final reminder one week before our cut-off, explaining what happens after it (extension, later appointment).
5. Thank-you email after filing, with how to reach us during the year.

For each email give: subject line (under 50 characters), preview text, body (under 180 words), one clear call to action.
Rules: never ask clients to email Social Security numbers or tax documents as plain attachments; point them to [SECURE METHOD]. No tax advice or promised refund amounts. Mark anything I must check with {VERIFY}.

## After-hours support auto-reply prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/after-hours-support-auto-reply/
Category: Customer service
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Write after-hours and holiday support auto-replies for email, chat and SMS that set clear response times, offer self-help and route urgent issues.

Prompt:

Act as a customer support lead writing automated replies.

Company: [COMPANY NAME]
Business hours and time zone: [E.G. MON–FRI 9:00–18:00 EST]
Channels: [EMAIL / LIVE CHAT / SMS / SOCIAL DM / PHONE VOICEMAIL]
Typical first response time when we're back: [E.G. WITHIN 4 BUSINESS HOURS]
Self-help resources: [E.G. HELP CENTRE URL, ORDER TRACKING PAGE, STATUS PAGE]
Urgent issues and what to do: [E.G. OUTAGES — CHECK STATUS PAGE; SECURITY ISSUES — EMAIL SECURITY@; NONE]
Upcoming holidays or closures: [DATES]
Brand voice: [E.G. WARM AND CASUAL / PROFESSIONAL]

Write:
1. An after-hours email auto-reply (subject line + body).
2. A short chat widget message for when no agents are online, with an option to leave a message.
3. An SMS reply under 160 characters.
4. A social media DM auto-reply.
5. A voicemail greeting script (under 30 seconds).
6. A holiday closure version for each of the above, with dates as placeholders.
7. A weekend version that sets expectations for Monday.
8. Rules for when to send (and not repeat) the auto-reply to the same customer.

Each message should: confirm receipt, give a specific response time, offer 1–2 self-help links, and explain urgent options if any. No promises we can't keep.

## Antique shop marketing prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/antique-shop-marketing/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Market an antique shop or vintage mall with item story posts, new-arrival alerts, collector email lists, event ideas and online listing copy that sells.

Prompt:

Act as a retail marketing advisor for antique and vintage dealers.

Shop: [SHOP NAME], [TOWN], [SINGLE DEALER / MULTI-DEALER ANTIQUE MALL]
Specialties: [E.G. MID-CENTURY FURNITURE, VICTORIAN JEWELLERY, VINTAGE SIGNS, PRIMITIVES, BOOKS]
Customers: [E.G. COLLECTORS, INTERIOR DESIGNERS, TOURISTS, YOUNG BUYERS FURNISHING HOMES]
Where we sell: [SHOP / OWN WEBSITE / ONLINE MARKETPLACES / SOCIAL MEDIA]
Problem to solve: [E.G. SLOW WEEKDAYS, LARGE PIECES NOT MOVING, NOT REACHING YOUNGER BUYERS]

Create:
1. A template for an "item story" post (what it is, era, maker if known, condition, why it's special, price or "ask").
2. Ten post ideas across formats (styling a room with antiques, "guess the use" posts, before/after restorations, dealer spotlights).
3. A collector wish-list sign-up and a new-arrivals email template.
4. Four event ideas (appraisal day with a qualified appraiser, themed sale, design night, holiday open house) with how to run each.
5. Listing copy template for online sales with measurements, condition notes and shipping info.
6. Ideas to sell large furniture faster (staging, delivery partners, designer outreach).
7. A short "about us" story for the website and signage.

Never claim a maker, age or value unless confirmed; use words like "attributed to" or "appears to be" where unsure.

## App icon design image prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/app-icon-design-image/
Category: Image
Works with: GPT Image, Midjourney, Flux and Ideogram
Published: 2026-11-27

Generate app icon concepts that read at small sizes, with one bold symbol, a strong color and a rounded-square layout, shown on a home screen mockup.

Prompt:

App icon design for "[APP NAME]", a [WHAT THE APP DOES] app for [AUDIENCE].

Concept: one bold, simple symbol representing [CORE IDEA, E.G. A LEAF COMBINED WITH A CHECKMARK].
Style: [FLAT MINIMAL / SOFT 3D WITH GENTLE SHADOW / GLYPH ON GRADIENT / OUTLINED], clean geometric shapes.
Colors: background [COLOR OR TWO-COLOR GRADIENT], symbol [COLOR], high contrast.
Shape: square canvas filling the frame edge to edge (the platform will round the corners), symbol centred with even padding.
Readability: must still be recognisable at 48 x 48 pixels; no text, no letters (unless a single letter is the concept: "[LETTER]"), no thin lines, no small details.
Show: four different concepts side by side at large size, then the strongest one on a phone home screen mockup between generic app icons.
No real brand logos, no watermark.

## App promo video with a phone mockup prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/app-promo-phone-mockup-video/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-27

Create a short app promo video with a floating phone mockup, smooth camera moves and screen-safe framing for app store previews, ads and launch posts.

Prompt:

Product video of a modern smartphone, [DURATION, E.G. 6–8 SECONDS], [9:16 / 16:9 / 1:1].

Phone: a [BLACK / WHITE / SILVER] modern smartphone with thin bezels, no brand logos.
Screen: [SOLID BRIGHT GREEN SCREEN FOR REPLACEMENT / SOLID WHITE / A SIMPLE ABSTRACT GRADIENT], evenly lit, no reflections covering it.
Scene: [MINIMAL PASTEL STUDIO / DARK BACKGROUND WITH SOFT COLORED RIM LIGHT / LIFESTYLE DESK WITH PLANTS / ABSTRACT 3D SHAPES IN BRAND COLORS: [COLORS]]
Motion: the phone [FLOATS AND ROTATES SLOWLY FROM ANGLED TO FACING CAMERA / RISES INTO FRAME / TILTS GENTLY]
Camera: [SMOOTH ORBIT / SLOW PUSH-IN], ends with the screen facing the camera, filling about [50]% of the frame and held still for the last 2 seconds.
Lighting: soft studio light, subtle reflections on the phone edges.
Mood: [CLEAN AND PREMIUM / PLAYFUL AND BRIGHT]
No hands, no text, no interface elements, no logos.

## Local SEO plan prompt for appliance repair companies

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/appliance-repair-local-seo/
Category: SEO
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Build a local SEO plan for an appliance repair business, with service and brand-agnostic pages, Google Business Profile fixes and review steps.

Prompt:

You are a local SEO consultant for home service companies.

Business: [NAME], appliance repair in [CITY] and [SERVICE AREA TOWNS].
Appliances we repair: [E.G. REFRIGERATORS, WASHERS, DRYERS, OVENS, DISHWASHERS]
Brands we are trained or authorised for: [LIST ONLY TRUE ONES, OR "ALL MAJOR BRANDS" IF ACCURATE]
Service details: [SAME-DAY AVAILABILITY, DIAGNOSTIC FEE, WARRANTY ON PARTS AND LABOUR]
Website pages now: [LIST]
Google Business Profile status: [CATEGORIES, PHOTOS COUNT, REVIEW COUNT, POSTING FREQUENCY]
Top competitors in the map results: [NAMES AND WHAT THEY DO WELL]

Deliver:
1. Recommended Google Business Profile primary and secondary categories, services list and a 750-character description.
2. A site structure: one page per appliance type, and city pages only for towns we truly serve, with internal links.
3. A full outline for the [APPLIANCE] repair page: title tag, meta description, H1, sections (common problems, our process, pricing/diagnostic fee, brands, service area, FAQ with 6 questions), and a call to action.
4. A review routine: when technicians ask, a text template, and how to reply to reviews.
5. 6 Google Business Profile post ideas tied to seasonal appliance problems.
6. Local citation checklist: where to keep name, address and phone consistent.
7. A 90-day priority list.

Do not suggest fake addresses, keyword-stuffed business names or review incentives. Mention trademark care when using appliance brand names.

## ChatGPT prompts for art teachers: lesson plans

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/art-lesson-plan-elementary/
Category: Education
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Plan an elementary art lesson with a clear objective, artist link, materials list, step-by-step demo, differentiation and a simple rubric.

Prompt:

You are an experienced elementary art teacher and curriculum planner.

Plan an art lesson:
- Grade: [GRADE]
- Class length and number of sessions: [E.G. 45 MINUTES X 2 SESSIONS]
- Class size: [NUMBER]
- Skill or element of art to teach: [E.G. WARM AND COOL COLORS / OVERLAPPING SHAPES / TEXTURE / SYMMETRY]
- Theme or link (optional): [E.G. SEASONS, A CLASSROOM TOPIC, A CULTURAL CELEBRATION]
- Artist or art movement to connect (or "suggest"): [ARTIST OR "SUGGEST"]
- Supplies I actually have: [LIST]
- Standards to reference: [E.G. NATIONAL CORE ARTS STANDARDS / LOCAL STANDARDS / NONE]
- Students needing support: [E.G. FINE MOTOR NEEDS, ENGLISH LEARNERS]

Include:
1. Learning objective in student-friendly "I can" language.
2. Vocabulary (max 5 words) with kid-friendly definitions.
3. A 5-minute hook and a short discussion about the artist's work (describe what to show; no copyrighted images needed).
4. Step-by-step demo and student work time, with minutes for each part, for every session.
5. Differentiation: simpler version, extension challenge, and supports for the needs listed.
6. Set-up and clean-up routine for this material.
7. A closing reflection or gallery walk with 3 questions.
8. A 4-level rubric (3 criteria) and a one-line note home to families.

## Membership drive campaign for associations

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/association-membership-drive/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Plan a membership drive for an association or club with segment value props, email and social copy, a referral offer and renewal reminders.

Prompt:

Act as a membership marketing manager. Plan a membership drive.

Organisation: [NAME, TYPE E.G. PROFESSIONAL ASSOCIATION, SPORTS CLUB, CHAMBER, ALUMNI GROUP]
Membership tiers and prices: [TIERS, PRICES, WHAT EACH INCLUDES]
Current members and retention: [NUMBERS, IF KNOWN]
Target segments: [E.G. STUDENTS, EARLY-CAREER PROFESSIONALS, SMALL BUSINESSES, LAPSED MEMBERS]
Main benefits members actually use: [EVENTS, TRAINING, DISCOUNTS, NETWORKING, ADVOCACY, PUBLICATIONS]
Campaign period and goal: [DATES, E.G. 150 NEW MEMBERS]
Channels: [EMAIL LIST, SOCIAL, EVENTS, PARTNERS, PRINT]
Budget for incentives: [AMOUNT OR NONE]

Deliver:
1. A value proposition for each segment: the problem they have and the 3 benefits that solve it.
2. Campaign timeline (weekly) with channels and messages.
3. Emails: invitation to prospects, win-back to lapsed members, member-get-member ask, last-chance reminder. Subject lines included.
4. Six social posts and a short member testimonial request (to collect real quotes, not invented ones).
5. A referral offer that's simple to explain and doesn't devalue membership.
6. A welcome sequence for new members (first 30 days) to make them active early.
7. Renewal reminders at 60, 30 and 7 days, plus a grace-period message.
8. What to measure and a simple results table.

SITTING ON A SWING / FISHING / READING A BOOK / HOLDING A RED BALLOON / WATERING A PLANT], in [UNEXPECTED SETTING, E.G. A SUNFLOWER FIELD AT SUNSET / A FLOODED LIBRARY / AN EMPTY DINER AT NIGHT / A SNOW-COVERED FOREST / ON A TINY ISLAND IN A SEA OF CLOUDS].

## Aurora borealis AI image prompt for night skies

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/aurora-borealis-landscape-image/
Category: Image
Works with: Midjourney, Flux, GPT Image and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Generate realistic northern lights landscapes with believable aurora colors, a strong foreground, reflections and night photography settings.

Prompt:

Night landscape photograph of the aurora borealis over [LOCATION TYPE, E.G. A FROZEN LAKE WITH SNOW-COVERED PINES / A FJORD WITH A SMALL RED FISHING CABIN / BLACK SAND BEACH WITH ICE BLOCKS / ARCTIC MOUNTAINS].

Aurora: [GREEN CURTAINS WITH FAINT PINK EDGES / SOFT GREEN ARC LOW ON THE HORIZON / BRIGHT CORONA OVERHEAD], natural colors, visible ribbon structure.
Foreground: [STRONG FOREGROUND ELEMENT, E.G. A LONE TREE / ROCKS IN SHALLOW WATER / A TENT GLOWING WARMLY], sharp and detailed.
Reflection: [AURORA REFLECTED IN STILL WATER / NO REFLECTION].
Sky: clear, many stars, [MOON OR NO MOON].
Person (optional): [TINY SILHOUETTE WITH A HEADLAMP / NONE].
Camera feel: wide-angle 14–20mm lens, long exposure, low noise, realistic night tones, slight cool white balance.
Mood: quiet, cold, still.
Aspect ratio [16:9 / 3:2 / 9:16].
No text, no watermark, no oversaturated neon colors.

## Auto detailing business marketing prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/auto-detailing-business-promotions/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Plan auto detailing promotions with package names, seasonal offers, before-and-after post captions and rebooking messages for repeat clients.

Prompt:

You are a marketing consultant for mobile and shop-based auto detailing businesses.

Business: [NAME], [MOBILE / SHOP] detailing in [AREA].
Services and prices: [E.G. EXPRESS WASH $X, FULL INTERIOR $Y, PAINT CORRECTION $Z, CERAMIC COATING FROM $W]
Typical clients: [E.G. BUSY PARENTS, LEASE RETURNS, CAR ENTHUSIASTS, FLEETS]
Slow months: [MONTHS]
Channels: [INSTAGRAM / FACEBOOK / GOOGLE BUSINESS PROFILE / TEXT LIST]
Booking method: [LINK OR PHONE]

Deliver:
1. Three clear packages (good / better / best) with names, what is included, time on the car and who each suits. Keep my prices.
2. A promotion for each season, plus one for my slow months, with terms (e.g. valid dates, vehicle size surcharges).
3. 10 captions for before-and-after photos (under 60 words each), each teaching one thing (pet hair, salt stains, swirl marks, headlight haze, odour).
4. A text and email to send 30, 60 or 90 days after a detail to rebook, by package.
5. A maintenance plan offer (monthly or quarterly) with a simple explanation of the value.
6. A short pitch to local businesses with company cars or dealerships.

Do not promise results like "like new" or "permanent protection"; describe what the service does. Ceramic coating claims should mention that durability depends on product and care.

## Backorder notice email prompt for online stores

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/backorder-notice-email/
Category: Customer service
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Write a backorder notice email that tells customers the new ship date, their options (wait, swap or refund) and how to choose in one click.

Prompt:

You write customer service emails for an online store.

Store: [STORE NAME], brand voice: [FRIENDLY / PREMIUM AND CALM / PLAYFUL]
Customer first name: [NAME]
Order number and item(s) on backorder: [ORDER, ITEM, QUANTITY]
Other items in the order: [SHIPPING NOW / HELD UNTIL COMPLETE / NONE]
Reason (short and true): [E.G. SUPPLIER DELAY / DEMAND HIGHER THAN EXPECTED]
New estimated ship date: [DATE OR RANGE]
Customer options: [WAIT / SWAP FOR SIMILAR ITEM / PARTIAL SHIPMENT / FULL REFUND]
Goodwill gesture, if any: [E.G. FREE SHIPPING UPGRADE, DISCOUNT CODE — OR "NONE"]
How the customer chooses: [REPLY TO EMAIL / LINKS / ACCOUNT PAGE]
Deadline for choosing before we apply the default: [DATE AND DEFAULT OPTION]

Write:
1. Subject line (clear, not alarming) and preview text.
2. The email: apology in one line, what is delayed and why, new date, options as clear buttons or numbered choices, what happens if they do nothing, goodwill gesture, and contact details. Under 180 words.
3. A short SMS version (under 300 characters).
4. A follow-up if the date slips again, with a stronger apology and an easy refund.
5. A "your item has shipped" message for backordered items.
6. 3 saved replies for customers who reply upset.

Never promise a date we have not confirmed. Make refunds as easy to choose as waiting.

## BANT lead qualification questions and scoring

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/bant-lead-qualification/
Category: Sales
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Get natural BANT discovery questions for budget, authority, need and timing, plus a simple lead scoring sheet and next steps for each score.

Prompt:

Act as a sales enablement manager. Build a BANT qualification kit for my team.

Product and price range: [WHAT WE SELL, TYPICAL DEAL SIZE]
Typical buyer: [JOB TITLES, COMPANY SIZE, INDUSTRY]
Who usually signs: [E.G. CFO ABOVE $20K, TEAM LEAD BELOW]
Typical sales cycle: [E.G. 2–6 WEEKS]
Main problems we solve: [PROBLEMS]
Where leads come from: [INBOUND FORM, EVENTS, OUTBOUND]

Create:
1. For each BANT element, 4 natural questions that don't sound like a checklist (e.g. instead of "What's your budget?"), plus what a strong, weak and unclear answer sounds like.
2. Follow-up questions when the answer is vague.
3. A scoring sheet: 0–3 points per element with clear criteria, and total-score bands (pursue now, nurture, disqualify).
4. Recommended next step for each band, including a short follow-up email for nurture leads.
5. Red flags that should override the score.
6. A short note on when BANT isn't enough (e.g. complex deals with many stakeholders) and which extra questions to add.
7. CRM fields to record the answers.

## Bed and breakfast marketing plan prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/bed-and-breakfast-marketing/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Build a bed and breakfast marketing plan with a guest profile, direct booking copy, local packages, email ideas and review replies that fill rooms.

Prompt:

Act as a hospitality marketing consultant for independent inns.

Property: [B&B NAME], [NUMBER] rooms in [TOWN / REGION]
What's special: [E.G. 1890S FARMHOUSE, HOMEMADE BREAKFAST WITH LOCAL EGGS, WALK TO WINERIES, PET-FRIENDLY ROOM]
Typical guests now: [E.G. COUPLES ON WEEKEND GETAWAYS, WEDDING GUESTS, HIKERS]
Guests I want more of: [E.G. MIDWEEK REMOTE WORKERS, SMALL RETREATS]
Where bookings come from: [E.G. 70% BOOKING SITES, 30% DIRECT]
Busy and quiet periods: [E.G. FULL IN OCTOBER, EMPTY IN JANUARY]
Nearby attractions and partners: [E.G. VINEYARDS, STATE PARK, ANTIQUE SHOPS, WEDDING VENUE]
Budget and time per week: [AMOUNT / HOURS]

Create:
1. Two guest personas with what they search for and what makes them book.
2. Homepage copy: headline, short story of the house and hosts, room highlights, and a direct-booking benefit (for example a perk that booking sites don't offer).
3. Three packages for quiet periods with names, what's included and a short description.
4. A 12-week plan (table): week, action, channel, time needed.
5. A pre-arrival email, a post-stay thank-you email with a return-guest offer, and a seasonal newsletter.
6. Replies to one glowing review and one critical review.
7. Partnership pitch to a local business for a joint offer.

Keep it warm and personal, and don't invent awards or guest quotes.

## Bike shop marketing prompt for every season

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/bike-shop-seasonal-promotions/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Plan bike shop marketing by season, with service tune-up campaigns, group ride posts, winter storage offers and emails that bring riders back.

Prompt:

You are a marketing advisor for independent bicycle shops.

Shop: [NAME] in [TOWN], selling [E.G. ROAD, GRAVEL, MOUNTAIN, E-BIKES, KIDS' BIKES] and offering [SERVICES, E.G. TUNE-UPS, BIKE FITS, REPAIRS, RENTALS].
Service menu and prices: [LIST]
Customers: [E.G. COMMUTERS, WEEKEND ROAD RIDERS, FAMILIES, MOUNTAIN BIKERS, TOURISTS]
Community activities: [GROUP RIDES, CLINICS, LOCAL TRAILS OR CLUBS WE SUPPORT]
Channels: [EMAIL LIST, INSTAGRAM, FACEBOOK, GOOGLE BUSINESS PROFILE, IN-STORE]
Slowest months: [MONTHS]

Deliver:
1. A 12-month calendar with one main campaign per season (e.g. spring tune-up, summer adventure, autumn commuter safety, winter storage and indoor training).
2. For the spring tune-up campaign: an email, 3 social posts and in-store sign wording, with a booking deadline approach that spreads work across weeks.
3. 6 educational posts riders will save (chain care, tyre pressure, e-bike battery care in cold weather, fitting a kids' helmet).
4. A group ride or clinic announcement and a recap post template.
5. A winter offer to keep the service bench busy (storage, overhaul bundles, bike fit), with clear terms.
6. A post-purchase email series for new bike buyers: day 1 (setup tips), week 4 (free check-up reminder if we offer one), month 6 (service reminder).
7. 3 metrics to track per campaign.

Use my prices exactly. No invented discounts or awards.

## Bowling alley marketing ideas prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/bowling-alley-marketing/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Get bowling alley marketing ideas for leagues, parties, corporate events, weeknight specials and social content that fills lanes in quiet hours.

Prompt:

Act as a marketing manager for a family entertainment and bowling centre.

Venue: [NAME], [CITY], [NUMBER] lanes
Extras: [E.G. ARCADE, BAR AND GRILL, LASER TAG, BILLIARDS, PRIVATE PARTY ROOM]
Current offers: [E.G. CLOSE-OUT BOWLING, KIDS BOWL FREE IN SUMMER, LEAGUES]
Customers: [E.G. FAMILIES, TEENS, LEAGUE BOWLERS, COMPANIES, DATE NIGHTS]
Quiet times to fill: [E.G. MONDAY–THURSDAY DAYTIME, SUNDAY EVENINGS]
Channels: [WEBSITE, SOCIAL MEDIA, EMAIL, LOCAL SCHOOLS, BUSINESS GROUPS]

Create:
1. Five weeknight or daytime offers with names, rules and target audience (e.g. retirees, homeschool groups, students).
2. A league recruitment plan with copy for a flyer, social post and email, including beginner-friendly leagues.
3. A corporate event package page: team-building angle, packages, catering, booking steps.
4. Birthday party copy and a follow-up email for inquiries.
5. A 12-week social media calendar with post ideas (strike videos, staff picks from the menu, theme nights).
6. Three theme night ideas (e.g. glow bowling, retro music night, trivia and bowling).
7. A loyalty or punch card idea.
8. How to measure which offers fill quiet lanes.

## Fishbone diagram root cause analysis

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/fishbone-root-cause-analysis/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Run a fishbone (Ishikawa) root cause analysis on any problem, with causes grouped by category, 5 Whys on the top suspects and a plan to test each one.

Prompt:

Act as a process improvement facilitator.

Problem statement: [DESCRIBE THE PROBLEM: WHAT, WHERE, WHEN, HOW OFTEN, SINCE WHEN]
Impact: [E.G. 12% OF ORDERS SHIP LATE, CUSTOMER COMPLAINTS UP]
Context: [TEAM, PROCESS, TOOLS, RECENT CHANGES]
What we already know or suspect: [NOTES, DATA, OBSERVATIONS]
Category set: [6M FOR MANUFACTURING: METHODS, MACHINES, MATERIALS, MEASUREMENT, MANPOWER, MOTHER NATURE / 4P FOR SERVICES: POLICIES, PROCEDURES, PEOPLE, PLANT / OR SUGGEST ONE]

Please:
1. Rewrite the problem statement so it is specific and free of assumed causes.
2. Build a fishbone diagram as an indented text outline: categories, then possible causes, then sub-causes.
3. Mark each cause as "supported by evidence", "plausible" or "unlikely", based on what I gave you.
4. Pick the top 3 likely root causes and run a 5 Whys chain on each.
5. For each top cause, say what data or test would confirm or rule it out.
6. Suggest a fix for each cause if confirmed, with an owner role and a way to measure success.
7. List questions I should ask the people closest to the process.

Don't treat guesses as facts. Separate what we know from what we suspect.

Extras needed: [E.G. MEDICAL TREATMENT CONSENT, PHOTO/VIDEO RELEASE, RULES ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, HEALTH DECLARATION]
How it's signed: [PAPER / ONLINE CHECKBOX AND SIGNATURE]

Draft a waiver with:
1. A clear title and a short plain-English summary at the top.
2. Description of the activity and its specific risks.
3. Assumption of risk.
4. Release and waiver of claims, written as clearly as possible.
5. Participant responsibilities and rules acknowledgement.
6. Health and fitness declaration.
7. Emergency medical treatment consent.
8. Optional photo/video release as a separate checkbox.
9. Minor participant section (if relevant).
10. Severability, governing law and signature block with date.

After the draft, list:
- Points that differ by jurisdiction (e.g. whether gross negligence can be waived, rules for minors).
- Questions for my lawyer.
Do not claim the waiver is guaranteed to be enforceable.

## Limerick writing prompt with correct rhythm

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/limerick-writer/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Write funny limericks about any person, pet or topic with the right AABBA rhyme and bouncy rhythm, plus clean versions for cards, toasts and classes.

Prompt:

Write limericks about: [TOPIC, PERSON OR PET, E.G. "MY COLLEAGUE DAVE WHO ALWAYS BURNS THE OFFICE POPCORN"]

Details to use: [E.G. NAME, HOMETOWN, HOBBIES, A FUNNY HABIT, AN EVENT]
Occasion: [E.G. BIRTHDAY CARD, RETIREMENT TOAST, CLASS EXAMPLE, JUST FOR FUN]
Audience: [E.G. FAMILY, COWORKERS, CHILDREN]
Tone: [GENTLE TEASING / SILLY / CLEVER WORDPLAY]
Number of limericks: [E.G. 5]

Rules:
- Five lines, rhyme scheme AABBA.
- Lines 1, 2 and 5 have three stressed beats (about 8–9 syllables); lines 3 and 4 have two stressed beats (about 5–6 syllables).
- Bouncy anapestic rhythm (da-da-DUM), and a twist or punchline in the last line.
- Only true rhymes, no forced word order.
- Keep it kind: tease habits, not looks, weight, age or anything hurtful.

For each limerick, show the stressed syllables in CAPITALS on a second copy so I can check the rhythm. Then tell me which one reads best aloud and why.

[CATEGORY | COUNT OR VALUE]

## SPIN selling questions for your next sales call

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/spin-selling-discovery-questions/
Category: Sales
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-27

Build SPIN selling questions (situation, problem, implication, need-payoff) tailored to your product, buyer and deal stage, with follow-ups.

Prompt:

Act as a B2B sales coach who teaches the SPIN selling method.

Context:
- What I sell: [PRODUCT OR SERVICE] that helps with [CORE OUTCOME]
- Buyer: [JOB TITLE] at [COMPANY TYPE AND SIZE]
- What I already know about this account: [NOTES FROM CRM OR RESEARCH]
- Common problems our customers had before buying: [PROBLEMS]
- Call length: [MINUTES]

Write a SPIN question bank:
1. Situation questions (max 4): only things I could not find through research.
2. Problem questions (6): about difficulties, dissatisfaction and workarounds.
3. Implication questions (6): connect each problem to cost, time, risk, team morale or missed revenue. Show which problem each one follows.
4. Need-payoff questions (5): get the buyer to state the value of solving it in their own words.

For each question add one natural follow-up ("Tell me more about…", "What happened then?").
Then give:
- A suggested order for a [MINUTES]-minute call, with time for the buyer to talk.
- 3 signs the buyer is not a fit yet, and how to end the call politely with a next step.
- Questions to avoid because they sound like an interrogation or lead the witness.

## Weighted decision matrix prompt to compare options

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/weighted-decision-matrix/

Published: 2026-11-27

Build a weighted decision matrix that scores options against criteria you choose, tests how sensitive the result is and explains the trade-offs.

Prompt:

You are a strategy consultant who facilitates structured decisions.

Decision: [WHAT WE ARE DECIDING, E.G. WHICH CRM TO ADOPT]
Options: [OPTION A, OPTION B, OPTION C...]
Who is affected: [TEAMS OR PEOPLE]
Deadline and constraints: [BUDGET, MUST-HAVES, TIMING]

Criteria and weights (total 100), or write "suggest" and I will review:
[CRITERION | WEIGHT, E.G. TOTAL COST | 25]

What we know about each option:
[PASTE FACTS, QUOTES, DEMO NOTES, TEAM OPINIONS]

Please:
1. If I wrote "suggest", propose 5–7 criteria with weights and a one-line reason for each, then stop and wait for my approval.
2. Separate must-haves (pass/fail) from weighted criteria. Remove any option that fails a must-have and say why.
3. Score each remaining option 1–5 per criterion, with a short justification and a confidence level (high/medium/low) based on the facts I gave.
4. Show the matrix as a table with weighted scores and totals (show the arithmetic).
5. Sensitivity check: would the winner change if any single weight moved by 10 points? Which criterion decides the outcome?
6. List the 3 low-confidence scores worth verifying before deciding.
7. Write a 5-sentence recommendation I can share with stakeholders, including the main risk of the chosen option.

5. A reply for "can you give us a discount?" that protects value but offers a reasonable option.

Tone: helpful and professional. Under 150 words each. No pressure tactics or vague threats of service loss.

## Six thinking hats for a decision

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/six-thinking-hats-decision/
Category: Productivity
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-26

Analyse a decision from six angles — facts, feelings, risks, benefits, ideas and process — using the six thinking hats method, then pick a next step.

Prompt:

Use the six thinking hats method to help me think through a decision.

Decision or problem: [E.G. SHOULD WE MOVE TO A 4-DAY WEEK? SHOULD I ACCEPT A ROLE ABROAD?]
Context: [BACKGROUND, CONSTRAINTS, DEADLINE]
Options I'm considering: [LIST]
Who is affected: [PEOPLE OR TEAMS]

Go through each hat separately, with 4–6 points each:
- White hat: facts we know, facts we're missing, and how to get them.
- Red hat: gut feelings and emotions — mine and likely others' — without justification.
- Black hat: risks, weaknesses, what could go wrong.
- Yellow hat: benefits and best realistic outcomes.
- Green hat: creative alternatives, including options I haven't listed.
- Blue hat: summary, what matters most, a recommended decision or experiment, and the next 3 steps.

## Survey question bias review

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/survey-question-bias-review/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-26

Check a draft survey for leading, double-barrelled and loaded questions, unbalanced scales and order effects, with neutral rewrites.

Prompt:

Act as a survey methodologist. Review my draft survey for bias and clarity.

Purpose of the survey: [WHAT DECISION IT WILL INFORM]
Audience: [WHO WILL ANSWER, HOW THEY'LL BE RECRUITED]
Mode: [ONLINE / PHONE / IN PERSON], estimated length: [MINUTES]
Draft questions with answer options:
[PASTE SURVEY]

For each question, check for:
- leading or loaded wording
- double-barrelled questions (two topics in one)
- unbalanced or overlapping answer scales, missing "not applicable" or "don't know"
- jargon or ambiguous terms
- assumptions the respondent may not share
- memory demands that are unrealistic
- sensitive topics that need softer wording or an opt-out

Output:
1. A table: question number, problem found, why it biases results, neutral rewrite.
2. Order effects: questions that may influence later answers, and a better order.
3. Questions to cut because they don't serve the stated purpose.
4. A short pilot test plan (who, how many, what to watch for).
Leave questions without problems marked "OK".

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/wardley-map-strategy/

Published: 2026-11-26

Prompt:

Main user and their need: [WHO, WHAT THEY'RE TRYING TO ACHIEVE]

Strategic question: [E.G. WHAT SHOULD WE BUILD IN-HOUSE? WHERE CAN WE DIFFERENTIATE?]

## A/B Test Plan With a Clear Hypothesis

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/ab-test-plan-hypothesis/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

Plan an A/B test before you launch it — hypothesis, primary metric, sample size inputs, run time and decision rules — to avoid misleading results.

Prompt:

Write an A/B test plan.

What I want to change: [e.g. shorter signup form, new pricing page headline]
Page or channel: [WHERE]
Why I think it will work (evidence): [EVIDENCE, e.g. session recordings, survey answers]
Current traffic per week to this page: [VISITORS]
Current conversion rate for the main goal: [RATE]
Smallest improvement worth acting on: [e.g. +10% relative]
Testing tool: [TOOL OR "not chosen"]

Include:
1. Hypothesis in the format: Because [evidence], we believe [change] will cause [effect] for [audience]. We'll know when [metric] moves by [amount].
2. One primary metric, 2 guardrail metrics (things that must not get worse) and their definitions.
3. Sample size: explain the inputs (baseline rate, minimum detectable effect, significance, power), give a rough estimate per variant and the expected run time with my traffic. Show the formula or say which calculator to check it with.
4. Run rules: minimum full weeks, no peeking decisions, what to do with outliers.
5. Decision rules: ship, iterate or drop, based on outcomes.
6. Risks (seasonality, novelty effect, tracking issues) and how to check them before launch.

Learn how to write AI art prompts with a tutor that critiques your prompts layer by layer and gives small practice exercises to improve.

Prompt:

Be my AI art prompt tutor.

My level: [BEGINNER / SOME EXPERIENCE]
Generator I use: [MIDJOURNEY / FLUX / GPT IMAGE / GEMINI / OTHER]
The image I wanted: [DESCRIBE YOUR IDEA]
My prompt: [YOUR PROMPT]
What came out and what I didn't like: [RESULT]

1. Review my prompt against 7 layers: subject, action/pose, setting, composition/camera, lighting, medium/style, color and mood. For each layer: present, weak or missing.
2. Explain the 2 changes that would help most, and why the model behaved as it did.
3. Rewrite my prompt in my generator's style, then show a shorter version.
4. Give me one practice exercise: a small idea to prompt, focusing on the layer I'm weakest at, with a hint.
5. A 7-line cheat sheet I can keep.

Describe styles with techniques and eras, not living artists' names.

Category: Productivity
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

Learn how to write AI prompts with a coach that asks you questions first, then writes a better prompt and explains each improvement it made.

Prompt:

Act as my prompt-writing coach.

My goal: [WHAT YOU WANT THE AI TO DO]
My first attempt at a prompt: [YOUR PROMPT OR "none yet"]
Where I'll use it: [CHATGPT / CLAUDE / GEMINI / IMAGE TOOL / OTHER]

Step 1: Ask me up to 5 short questions that would most improve the result (audience, purpose, format, examples, constraints). Wait for my answers.
Step 2: Write an improved prompt in one copy-ready block.
Step 3: Explain each improvement in one line, naming the technique (e.g. giving context, setting a format, adding an example, asking it to check its work).

## AI Voice Prompt for Natural Voiceovers

Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

Prompt:

Prepare a voiceover for an AI voice tool.

Video type and audience: [e.g. 60-second product explainer for small business owners]
Feeling the voice should create: [e.g. calm and trustworthy, upbeat, documentary]
Voice preferences: [AGE RANGE, GENDER OR NEUTRAL, ACCENT, PITCH]
Target length: [SECONDS]
Script: [PASTE SCRIPT]

1. A voice description in 2–3 sentences I can use to design or choose a voice (tone, texture, pace, accent, energy). No celebrity names.
2. Edit the script for the ear: shorter sentences, no tongue-twisters, numbers and abbreviations written the way they should be spoken.
3. Mark the script: [pause] for short breaks, *word* for emphasis, and a short direction before each section (e.g. "warmer, slower").
4. Estimate the read time and cut lines if it runs long.
5. List 3 lines that are most likely to sound unnatural and an alternative for each.

Keep the meaning of the script; don't add claims.

## First Principles Thinking Prompt for Hard Problems

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/first-principles-problem-breakdown/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

Break a hard business problem down to first principles — facts, assumptions and constraints — and rebuild fresh solutions instead of copying others.

Prompt:

Use first principles thinking on this problem.

Problem or goal: [e.g. our delivery cost per order is too high to be profitable]
Current approach and why we do it this way: [CURRENT APPROACH]
What we know for sure (numbers, constraints): [FACTS]
What competitors or the industry usually do: [CONVENTION]

1. Restate the problem as the underlying need, without assuming a solution.
2. List every belief behind the current approach. Label each as Fact (verifiable), Assumption (could be wrong) or Convention (done because others do it). Explain how to verify each assumption.
3. Break the problem into its basic components (cost elements, steps, customer needs) and estimate what each would cost or take if built from scratch. Mark estimates clearly.
4. Rebuild: 4 solutions that start from the components, including at least one that breaks a convention.
5. For each solution: what must be true for it to work, the biggest risk, and a small test.
6. Recommend which assumption to test first and why.

Ask me questions if a key fact is missing instead of inventing it.

How long can a ChatGPT prompt be? When your document is too long, use this chunking prompt to process it in parts and merge one accurate summary.

Prompt:

I'm going to send you a long document in several parts. Follow this process.

Document type and goal: [e.g. 80-page contract — find obligations and deadlines]
Number of parts: [N]
What to extract from each part: [e.g. key points, dates, numbers, risks, open questions]

For each part I send (labelled PART 1 of N, PART 2 of N...):
- Reply only with "Received PART X" and a numbered list of extracted notes, each tagged with the part and section heading.
- Don't summarize the whole document yet.
- Note anything that seems to continue from or into another part.

When I write "ALL PARTS SENT":
1. Merge the notes into one answer to my goal, grouped by theme.
2. Cite the part and section for every point.
3. List contradictions or gaps between parts.
4. List anything you're unsure about rather than guessing.

## Prompt Engineering Examples With 5 Techniques

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/prompt-engineering-techniques-compare/
Category: Productivity
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

See ChatGPT prompt engineering examples on your own task — zero-shot, few-shot, role, step-by-step and structured output — and compare the results.

Prompt:

Show me prompt engineering examples using my task.

My task: [e.g. classify customer emails by urgency, write product descriptions, summarize meeting notes]
Sample input I'll test with: [PASTE ONE REAL EXAMPLE]
What a good output looks like: [DESCRIPTION OR EXAMPLE]

Write 5 versions of a prompt for this task:
1. Zero-shot: a clear direct instruction.
2. Few-shot: the instruction plus 2–3 example input/output pairs (create realistic examples marked as samples).
3. Role prompting: assign a relevant expert role with standards to follow.
4. Step-by-step: ask the model to work through defined steps and check its answer before giving the final output.
5. Structured output: a strict format (JSON or table) with field definitions.

For each version: the full prompt in a code block, what it improves, when it's worth the extra length, and its weak spot.
Then combine the best parts into one final prompt, and give me a 3-question checklist to compare the outputs when I test them.

## Critique a research paper before you cite it

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/research-paper-critique/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

Check a study's question, method, sample, results and limitations in plain English, so you know how much weight to give it before citing.

Prompt:

Act as a methods-minded research mentor. Help me critically appraise a paper.

Paper: [TITLE, AUTHORS, YEAR, JOURNAL]
Text: [PASTE THE ABSTRACT AND METHODS, RESULTS AND DISCUSSION SECTIONS]
Why I want to cite it: [THE CLAIM YOU WANT TO SUPPORT]
My field and level: [E.G. UNDERGRADUATE PSYCHOLOGY, MARKETING ANALYST]

1. Summarise the research question, design and main finding in 3 sentences.
2. Assess: sample (size, how chosen, who is missing), design (and whether it can show cause or only association), measures, controls or comparison groups, statistics reported (effect sizes and confidence intervals, not just p-values), and conflicts of interest or funding.
3. List the limitations the authors admit and any they don't mention.
4. Say whether the paper supports the specific claim I want to make, partly supports it, or doesn't, and suggest more accurate wording for my citation.
5. Suggest what kind of additional evidence would strengthen the claim.

Base everything on the text I provided. If a section is missing, say what you can't judge.

Category: Sales

Published: 2026-11-25

Practice sales calls with ChatGPT playing a realistic buyer who pushes back, then get scored feedback on discovery, objections and next steps.

Prompt:

Let's role-play a sales call. You are the buyer; I am the seller.

What I sell: [PRODUCT OR SERVICE AND PRICE RANGE]
Buyer role and company: [e.g. operations manager at a 60-person logistics firm]
Call type: [COLD CALL / DISCOVERY / DEMO / NEGOTIATION]
Difficulty: [EASY / REALISTIC / HARD]
Hidden facts about the buyer (don't reveal unless I ask good questions): [e.g. contract with competitor ends in 3 months, CFO must approve]
Objections to raise: [e.g. price, timing, "send me an email"]

## SCAMPER Brainstorm Prompt for New Product Ideas

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/scamper-idea-brainstorm/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

Run the SCAMPER method with AI on any product, service or process and get scored ideas for each of the seven lenses, plus the best three to test.

Prompt:

Run a SCAMPER brainstorm on this.

What we're improving: [PRODUCT, SERVICE OR PROCESS]
Who it's for: [CUSTOMERS OR USERS]
Current problem or goal: [e.g. sales are flat, onboarding takes too long]
Constraints: [BUDGET, TIME, TECH, BRAND LIMITS]

For each of the 7 lenses (Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify/Magnify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Reverse/Rearrange):
- Ask the trigger question for that lens in plain words.
- Give 3 specific ideas for my case (not generic examples).

Then score every idea 1–5 on customer value, ease and fit with constraints, and show the top 8 in a table.
Pick the best 3 and for each give: a one-line concept, the main assumption, and a cheap test I can run in 2 weeks.
Flag ideas that are bold but risky separately rather than discarding them.

Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

Write a screenplay scene with ChatGPT in proper format — goals, conflict, subtext and action lines — then get notes on pacing and dialogue.

Prompt:

Help me write a screenplay scene.

Story so far (2–3 sentences): [CONTEXT]
Genre and tone: [e.g. grounded drama, dark comedy, thriller]
Characters in the scene (name, what they want right now, what they hide): [CHARACTERS]
Location and time: [e.g. INT. HOSPITAL PARKING GARAGE - NIGHT]
What must change by the end of the scene: [TURN]
Length: [e.g. 2–3 pages]

Step 1 — Scene plan: each character's goal, the obstacle, the turning point, the subtext (what's meant but not said).
Step 2 — The scene in standard screenplay format: scene heading, short action lines in present tense, character names in caps, dialogue, parentheticals only when needed.
Step 3 — Notes: where the dialogue is too on-the-nose, one line to cut, one visual moment to add, and whether the turn lands.

Rules: show emotion through action and choice, not explanation. Keep action lines to 3 lines or fewer.

## What Is an AI Prompt? Build Your First Good One

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/what-is-an-ai-prompt/
Category: Productivity
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-25

Learn what an AI prompt is by building one — this prompt turns your rough request into a clear prompt with role, task, context and output format.

Prompt:

I'm new to AI tools. Here is something I want help with, written the way I'd normally ask:

"[YOUR ROUGH REQUEST]"

Context about me: [WHO YOU ARE AND WHAT THIS IS FOR]

1. In 3 sentences, explain what an AI prompt is and why the wording changes the answer.
2. Rebuild my request as a clear prompt with these labelled parts: Role (who the AI should act as), Task (one clear job), Context (facts it needs), Constraints (length, tone, what to avoid), Output format (list, table, email, etc.).

5. Suggest 2 follow-up messages I can send after the first answer to improve it.

Keep the language simple and avoid jargon.

4. Recruitment criteria.
5. Analysis plan: similarity matrix, dendrogram, common group names, and how to handle items that people place inconsistently.
6. How to turn results into a draft navigation, and a follow-up tree test with 5–8 tasks.

When the drop started and how big it is: [DROP DETAILS]

## Write a research abstract from your paper

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/research-abstract-writer/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-23

A ChatGPT prompt that drafts a structured research abstract from your paper or notes, within the word limit and true to your actual findings.

Prompt:

You are an experienced academic editor. Draft an abstract for my research paper.

Field and target journal or conference: [FIELD AND VENUE]
Word limit and format (structured or unstructured, required headings): [LIMIT AND FORMAT]
Paper text or detailed notes (aim, methods, sample, results with numbers, conclusion): [PAPER OR NOTES]
Keywords required: [NUMBER OF KEYWORDS, or "none"]

Do this:
1. Write the abstract within the word limit, covering background, aim, methods, key results (with the numbers I gave), and conclusion.
2. Keep claims in line with the results: no causal claims from correlational data, no "proves" or "first ever" unless I said so.

4. Suggest keywords if needed.
5. Write a 2-sentence plain-language summary for non-experts.
6. List anything that seems unclear or missing in my notes (sample size, main outcome, limitations).

## Inclusion and exclusion criteria for a systematic review

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/systematic-review-inclusion-criteria/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-23

Draft inclusion and exclusion criteria for a systematic review with ChatGPT, using PICO, with screening questions and edge cases to agree on.

Prompt:

You are a research methods advisor. Help me define inclusion and exclusion criteria for a systematic review.

Research question: [QUESTION]
Field and type of review (systematic, scoping, rapid): [FIELD AND TYPE]
Framework to use: [PICO, PEO, SPIDER, or "suggest one"]
Study designs I expect: [DESIGNS]
Practical limits (languages, date range, databases): [LIMITS]

Create:

## Interpret A/B test results without mistakes

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/ab-test-results-interpretation/
Category: Data analysis
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt that interprets A/B test results, checks sample size and significance, and tells you whether to ship, stop or keep testing.

Prompt:

You are a data analyst who explains experiment results clearly.

What we tested and the hypothesis: [TEST AND HYPOTHESIS]
Primary metric and any secondary metrics: [METRICS]
Results per variant (visitors or users, conversions, revenue if relevant): [RESULTS]
Test dates and how traffic was split: [DATES AND SPLIT]
Minimum effect that would matter to the business: [MINIMUM EFFECT]

Do the following:
1. Calculate conversion rates, absolute and relative difference, and an approximate confidence interval and p-value. Show the formulas you used.
2. Check if the sample size is enough to detect the minimum effect; estimate how many more users are needed if not.
3. Flag possible problems: uneven split, too short a test, novelty effect, peeking, segment differences.
4. Review secondary metrics for side effects.
5. Recommendation: ship, do not ship, or keep testing, with the reason in plain language.
6. A three-sentence summary for non-technical stakeholders.
State clearly when results are inconclusive.

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/job-offer-letter-template/
Category: HR
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt that drafts a job offer letter with role, pay, start date and conditions in clear language, plus a friendly call script.

Prompt:

You are an HR partner drafting a job offer letter. This is a draft for review by our HR or legal team, not legal advice.

Company: [COMPANY]
Candidate name: [CANDIDATE]
Job title, team and manager: [ROLE DETAILS]
Employment type and location (remote, hybrid, office): [TYPE AND LOCATION]
Salary and pay frequency: [SALARY]
Bonus, equity or commission, if any: [VARIABLE PAY]
Benefits summary: [BENEFITS]
Start date and offer deadline: [DATES]
Conditions (background check, references, right to work, probation): [CONDITIONS]
Country or state: [JURISDICTION]

Write:
1. An offer letter under 350 words: warm opening, key terms in a clear list, conditions, how to accept, contact person.
2. A 2-minute script for the offer call, including how to respond if the candidate asks for time or negotiates.
3. A checklist of terms our HR or legal team should confirm for this jurisdiction.
Use the details exactly as given. Mark missing details as [ADD].

## Journalist query response that gets you quoted

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/journalist-query-response-pitch/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt that writes a fast, quotable response to a journalist's source request, with your expert answer, credentials and contact details.

Prompt:

You are a PR specialist helping an expert respond to a journalist's source request.

The journalist's request (paste it, including any requirements and deadline): [JOURNALIST REQUEST]
My name, title, company and why I'm qualified to comment: [MY CREDENTIALS]
My real views, experience or data on this topic (facts I can stand behind): [MY INPUT]
Links I can share (bio, headshot, relevant work): [LINKS]

Write a response email:
1. Subject line that mirrors the request topic.
2. One-line intro: who I am and why I'm relevant.
3. Answers to each question asked, written as 2–4 sentence quotes in my voice that a journalist can paste directly. Lead with the most interesting, specific point.
4. A short bio line with title and company.
5. Contact details and availability for a follow-up call.
Keep it under 250 words. Answer only what was asked, meet every stated requirement, and do not add claims, numbers or examples that aren't in my input.
Then list anything in the request I haven't covered.

## Letter of recommendation from your notes

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/letter-of-recommendation/
Category: Careers
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt for a letter of recommendation that turns your real examples of someone's work into a specific, credible reference letter.

Prompt:

You are helping me write a letter of recommendation. Use only the facts I give you.

My name, role and how I know the candidate (and for how long): [MY RELATIONSHIP]
Candidate's name and their role or class with me: [CANDIDATE]
What they are applying for (job, graduate program, scholarship) and what it values: [OPPORTUNITY]
Specific examples of their work, with results where I know them: [EXAMPLES]
Qualities I want to highlight: [QUALITIES]
Anything to address carefully (e.g., a short time working together): [NOTES]
Length and tone: [LENGTH AND TONE]

Write the letter with:
1. An opening that states who I am, how I know the candidate and a clear endorsement.
2. Two or three paragraphs, each built on one concrete example that shows a quality the opportunity values.
3. A comparison only if I provided one (e.g., "one of the best I have worked with in X years").
4. A closing with a strong recommendation and an offer to be contacted at {CONTACT DETAILS}.
Avoid clichés and empty adjectives. Do not invent achievements, numbers or comparisons.
Then list 3 questions I could ask the candidate to make the letter even stronger.

## Build a literature search strategy and keywords

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/literature-search-strategy/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt that builds a literature search strategy with concepts, synonyms, Boolean strings, databases and inclusion criteria.

Prompt:

You are an academic librarian who designs literature searches.

Research question: [QUESTION]
Field: [FIELD, e.g. nursing, education, economics]
Type of review: [TYPE, e.g. narrative, scoping, systematic]
Years, languages and study types to include: [LIMITS]
Databases I can access: [DATABASES, e.g. PubMed, Scopus, ERIC, Web of Science, Google Scholar]

Do this:
1. Break the question into 2–4 key concepts (use PICO or a similar framework if it fits).
2. For each concept, list synonyms, related terms, spelling variants and any controlled vocabulary terms I should look up (such as MeSH), marked "to verify".
3. Write one master Boolean search string with OR inside concepts and AND between them, using truncation and phrase marks.
4. Show how to adapt it for each of my databases (field tags and syntax), noting anything I should double-check in the database's help pages.
5. Draft inclusion and exclusion criteria.
6. Give a search log template (database, date, string, results, notes).
Do not list specific papers.

## Marketing budget plan and channel allocation

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/marketing-budget-allocation/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt that builds a marketing budget plan, splitting spend across channels by goal, with test budgets and rules for moving money.

Prompt:

You are a marketing director planning a budget.

Business and offer: [BUSINESS AND OFFER]
Total marketing budget and period: [BUDGET AND PERIOD]
Main goal and target (leads, sales, signups): [GOAL AND TARGET]
Average order value or deal size, and margin: [AOV OR DEAL SIZE, MARGIN]
Channels used so far and their results (spend, leads, sales, cost per result): [CHANNEL DATA]
Fixed costs (tools, agency fees, salaries if in budget): [FIXED COSTS]
Seasonality or key dates: [SEASONALITY]

Build a budget plan:
1. Split the budget into fixed costs, proven channels, and tests (suggest a % for tests and why).
2. A table by channel: monthly spend, expected result, cost per result, and the assumption behind it (from my data or marked as a guess).
3. A check: does the expected total reach my target? If not, say what would need to change.
4. Monthly phasing that follows seasonality.
5. Rules for reallocating: when to cut, pause or scale a channel, with thresholds.
6. A simple monthly tracking table.
Do not invent benchmark numbers; if I gave no data for a channel, treat it as a test.

## Mission, vision and values statement

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/mission-vision-values-statement/

You are a brand strategist helping a company write its mission, vision and values.

Company and what it does: [COMPANY]
Who we serve and the problem we solve: [CUSTOMERS AND PROBLEM]
What we do differently: [DIFFERENCE]
Where we want to be in 5–10 years: [AMBITION]
Examples of behavior we are proud of (real stories): [STORIES]

## Optimize a slow SQL query step by step

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/optimize-slow-sql-query/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt to optimize a slow SQL query using the query plan, schema and indexes, with a rewritten query and index suggestions to test.

Prompt:

You are a database performance engineer. Help me speed up this query.

Database and version (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, etc.): [DATABASE]
The slow query:
[QUERY]
Execution plan (EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE output): [EXECUTION PLAN]
Table definitions and existing indexes: [SCHEMA AND INDEXES]
Approximate row counts and how often tables change: [DATA SIZE]
Current run time and target: [TIMING]
How the query is used (report, API endpoint, batch job): [USAGE]

Deliver:
1. A plain-language explanation of the plan: where most of the time goes and why.
2. Specific problems found (full scans, bad joins, functions on indexed columns, implicit casts, N+1 patterns, sorting large sets, missing filters).
3. A rewritten query with comments explaining each change; results must stay identical.
4. Index suggestions with the exact CREATE INDEX statements, and the write and storage cost of each.
5. Other options if needed (caching, pagination, materialized views, partitioning).
6. How to test: what to compare in the new plan and how to confirm results match.
Do not assume columns or indexes that are not in the schema.

## Research hypotheses and how to test them

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/research-hypothesis-generator/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt that turns a research question into clear, testable hypotheses with variables, methods and the data needed to test each.

Prompt:

You are a research methods advisor.

Field and topic: [FIELD AND TOPIC]
Research question: [QUESTION]
What existing studies suggest (summarize what I know): [BACKGROUND]
Data or participants I can access: [DATA ACCESS]
Constraints (time, budget, ethics approval): [CONSTRAINTS]

Deliver:
1. A sharper version of the research question.
2. 3–5 testable hypotheses, each with null and alternative versions.
3. For each hypothesis: independent and dependent variables, how to measure them, likely confounders, and a suitable method (experiment, survey, observational, qualitative).
4. The data and sample needed, and a basic analysis approach.
5. Ethical considerations and limitations.
6. Which hypothesis is most feasible given my constraints, and why.
Do not cite specific studies unless I provided them; suggest search terms for the literature instead.

Topic and the problem it addresses: [TOPIC]

Planned methods, data, participants or sources: [METHODS]
Constraints (time, budget, access, ethics): [CONSTRAINTS]

## Check if a source is credible before you cite it

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/source-credibility-check/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-22

A ChatGPT prompt that checks whether a source is credible using authority, evidence, date, purpose and bias, then tells you how to cite or replace it.

Prompt:

You are a research librarian helping me judge whether a source is reliable.

What I am researching: [TOPIC OR QUESTION]
Where I will use the source (essay, report, article): [USE]
Source details (title, author, publisher, date, URL): [SOURCE DETAILS]
Key passage or claim I want to use: [PASTE PASSAGE]

Evaluate the source:
1. Authority: who wrote and published it, and what makes them qualified (or not). Say what I should verify myself.
2. Evidence: does the passage cite data, studies or primary sources? Are the claims specific and checkable?
3. Currency: is it recent enough for this topic?
4. Purpose and bias: is it informing, selling, persuading or campaigning? Who might benefit?
5. Corroboration: what kinds of sources should agree with this claim if it is true?
6. Verdict: use as is, use with a caveat, use only as an example of a viewpoint, or replace.
7. If I use it, suggest one neutral sentence that introduces the source fairly.
Do not invent facts about the author or publisher; if you do not know, tell me how to check.

5. An engagement plan: for each key stakeholder, the message that matters to them, channel, frequency, owner and the first conversation to have.
6. Signs that a stakeholder's stance is changing.
Mark where you are inferring stance rather than using what I told you.

## Advanced ChatGPT prompt that plans, drafts and self-checks

Category: Productivity
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

An advanced ChatGPT prompt that makes the AI clarify, plan, draft, critique against your criteria and revise before giving a final answer.

Prompt:

You will complete a task in stages. Do not skip stages.

Task: [TASK]
Audience and purpose: [AUDIENCE AND PURPOSE]
Material to use (notes, data, drafts): [MATERIAL]
Constraints (length, format, tone, deadline, must include/avoid): [CONSTRAINTS]
Quality criteria — how I will judge the result: [CRITERIA, e.g. accurate to the material, actionable, under 600 words, no jargon]

Stage 1 — Clarify: list up to 5 questions whose answers would change the result. Then stop and wait for my answers. If I say "proceed", make reasonable assumptions and list them.
Stage 2 — Plan: give a short outline and the approach you'll take, in under 120 words.
Stage 3 — Draft: write the full output.
Stage 4 — Critique: score the draft 1–5 on each of my criteria, quote the weakest parts and explain why they fall short. Check every factual claim against my material and flag anything not supported.
Stage 5 — Revise: produce the final version fixing every issue found. Then list what changed in 3 bullets.

Only the Stage 5 output is the final answer; keep earlier stages brief.

## API documentation from your code

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/api-documentation-from-code/

Published: 2026-11-21

Generate clear API reference docs from route handlers or code — endpoints, parameters, responses, errors and examples — ready for developers.

Prompt:

You are a technical writer for developer tools. Write API reference documentation from this code.

API purpose and audience: [API PURPOSE AND USERS]
Base URL and authentication method: [BASE URL AND AUTH]
Framework and language: [FRAMEWORK]
Code (routes, handlers, schemas, validation):
[CODE]

For each endpoint write:
1. Method, path and a one-line description of what it does.
2. Authentication and permissions required.
3. Path, query and body parameters in a table: name, type, required, description, constraints and defaults.

5. Error responses: status code, when it happens, example body.

- A short getting-started section with an authentication example.
- An OpenAPI 3 YAML snippet for the endpoints.
- A list of behaviours that are unclear from the code (for example, missing validation or undocumented error cases).

Document only what the code shows. Use realistic but obviously fake example values.

## Find the moat that protects your business

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/business-moat-analysis/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Assess which competitive advantages your business really has, how easy they are to copy, and what to build next to stay ahead.

Prompt:

You are a strategy consultant. Assess the competitive advantages of my business honestly.

Business, market and customers: [BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
What we believe makes us different: [CLAIMED STRENGTHS]
Main competitors and what they do well: [COMPETITORS]
Why customers choose us (evidence if any): [CUSTOMER REASONS]
Resources we have (team, data, partnerships, assets): [RESOURCES]

Do this:
1. Test each claimed strength: Do customers value it? Can a competitor copy it in under 12 months? Score each 1–5 on value and difficulty to copy, with reasons.
2. Check each moat type — switching costs, network effects, proprietary data or know-how, brand and trust, cost or scale advantages, regulation or exclusive access — and say whether we have it, could build it, or should ignore it.
3. Name our strongest current advantage and our biggest vulnerability.
4. Recommend one moat to invest in over the next 12 months, with 5 concrete actions and early signs that it is working.
5. List what a well-funded competitor would most likely do to beat us, and how we would respond.

Be direct. If a strength is weak, say so. Do not invent market data.

## Best ChatGPT prompts for business problems

Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

One of the best ChatGPT prompts for business owners: find the root cause of a problem, compare fixes and leave with a 30-day action plan.

Prompt:

Act as an experienced business consultant. Help me solve a problem in my business step by step.

Business: [WHAT YOU SELL, TO WHOM, TEAM SIZE]
The problem: [PROBLEM, E.G. "REPEAT ORDERS FELL OVER THE LAST 3 MONTHS"]
What I know for sure (data, dates, changes): [FACTS]
What I've already tried: [TRIED]
Constraints: [BUDGET, TIME, PEOPLE]

Work in this order:
1. Restate the problem in one measurable sentence.
2. List 6–8 possible root causes across product, price, customers, competitors, operations and team. For each, give the evidence for and against from my facts.
3. Pick the 3 most likely causes and give one cheap test for each that takes under a week.
4. For each cause, give 2 possible fixes with effort (low/medium/high) and expected impact.
5. Write a 30-day action plan: week by week, with an owner and a measure of success.

Ask me up to 5 questions first if key facts are missing. Do not invent numbers.

5. Give 3 outfit and 2 makeup or hair-color suggestions in this palette.

Where the prompt will run: [CLAUDE CHAT / CLAUDE PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS / API SYSTEM PROMPT]
Who the output is for: [AUDIENCE]
Inputs the prompt will receive each time: [INPUTS, e.g. a customer email, a CSV, meeting notes]
What a great output looks like: [GOOD OUTPUT]
Common mistakes to prevent: [MISTAKES]

4. Input placeholders wrapped in XML tags, e.g. <document>{DOCUMENT}</document>.
5. 1–2 examples in <example> tags if helpful.
6. An exact output format (headings, length, or a JSON shape).
7. What to do when the input is missing or unclear.

Then explain in 3 bullets why the prompt is built this way, and give one test input to try it on.

Get the best AI image prompts by diagnosing a weak prompt, finding what is vague or conflicting, and rewriting it with clear visual details.

Prompt:

You are an expert at writing prompts for AI image tools. Diagnose and fix my prompt.

Image tool: [MIDJOURNEY / FLUX / GPT IMAGE / OTHER]
My current prompt:
[PASTE PROMPT]

What I wanted: [DESCRIBE THE IMAGE YOU HAD IN MIND]
What I got instead: [DESCRIBE THE RESULT, OR UPLOAD IT]

Do this:
1. Score my prompt 1–5 on: subject clarity, composition, light, style consistency, detail level. One line of reason each.
2. List words that are vague, redundant or that conflict with each other.
3. Explain the most likely reason the result differed from what I wanted.
4. Rewrite the prompt: subject and action first, then setting, composition, light, style, colour, and tool-specific settings.
5. Give 2 alternative rewrites that each change one key decision (e.g. camera angle or style).
6. One rule I should remember for next time.

3. Camera and lens look (e.g. "35mm lens at eye level, shallow depth of field")
4. Light source and direction (e.g. "soft window light from the left")
5. Real-world imperfections: skin texture, flyaway hair, slight motion blur, everyday clutter, uneven surfaces
6. Colour grade (e.g. "natural, slightly warm, low contrast")
7. What to avoid: plastic skin, perfect symmetry, extra fingers, text

Then give 2 variations: one at a different time of day, one from a different camera angle.
Add tool syntax where needed (e.g. --ar and --style raw for Midjourney).

Character: [CHARACTER DESCRIPTION AND WHAT THEY ARE DOING]

Text type and audience: [TEXT TYPE AND AUDIENCE]
Purpose and tone required: [TONE]
Glossary (source term = required target term): [GLOSSARY]
Style rules (formality, units, dates, punctuation, brand names to keep): [STYLE RULES]
Source text:
[SOURCE]
Translation to review:
[TRANSLATION]

Review for: accuracy (omissions, additions, mistranslations), terminology and glossary compliance, consistency, grammar and spelling, register and tone, locale conventions (numbers, dates, currency), and fluency.

Output:
1. A table: segment #, source, current translation, suggested change, error type, severity (critical / major / minor), reason.
2. A list of terms used inconsistently.
3. Any source passages that are ambiguous, with the options and your recommended reading.
4. An overall quality note in 3 sentences.

Don't rewrite segments that are correct just for style preference; mark those "optional".

Category: SEO
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a personalised guest post pitch with tailored topic ideas, proof of your writing and a clear offer that editors are likely to answer.

Prompt:

You are an SEO outreach specialist. Write a guest post pitch.

Target site, editor name and audience: [SITE, EDITOR, AUDIENCE]
Recent articles on their site I read: [ARTICLES]
Topics they haven't covered well (from my research): [GAPS]
My expertise and writing samples: [EXPERTISE AND LINKS]
My website (for the author bio link): [MY SITE]

Write:
1. 3 subject lines.
2. A pitch under 150 words: a specific reference to their content, who I am, 3 topic ideas with working titles and one-line angles, what makes them useful to their readers, links to 2 samples, and a simple question.
3. A follow-up email for 6 days later.
4. A sample outline for the strongest topic.
5. A 2-sentence author bio with one natural link to my site.

No offers of payment for links, no mention of "do-follow". Focus on value to their readers.

## Image alt text in bulk for SEO and accessibility

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/image-alt-text-bulk/
Category: SEO
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write descriptive, concise alt text for many images at once that helps screen reader users and gives search engines useful context.

Prompt:

You are an accessibility and SEO specialist. Write alt text for these images.

Page topic and purpose: [PAGE TOPIC]
Main keyword (use only where it naturally fits): [KEYWORD]
Images — for each: file name, what it shows, and its role on the page (product, decorative, chart, step in a tutorial): [IMAGE LIST]

Rules:
1. Describe what matters in the image for this page, in under 125 characters.
2. Don't start with "image of" or "picture of".
3. For decorative images, recommend empty alt text (alt="") and say why.
4. For charts or infographics, give a short alt text plus a longer description to put in the page text.
5. Include the keyword in no more than a few images, only where accurate.
6. For products, include brand, product type and key visible feature such as colour.

Output a table: file name | alt text | notes.

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/internal-linking-plan/

Pages (URL, title, main keyword, one per line): [PAGE LIST]
Money or priority pages: [PAGES YOU MOST WANT TO RANK]

1. Group pages into topic clusters and pick a hub page for each.

## Jobs-to-be-done interview script

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/jobs-to-be-done-interview/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Get an interview guide that uncovers why customers really switched to your product, plus a template to analyse their answers.

Prompt:

You are a product researcher experienced in jobs-to-be-done interviews. Create an interview guide.

Product: [WHAT IT IS]
Who to interview: [RECENT CUSTOMERS WHO BOUGHT IN THE LAST X MONTHS / CUSTOMERS WHO LEFT]
What we want to learn: [E.G. WHY PEOPLE SWITCH FROM SPREADSHEETS]
Interview length: [MINUTES]

Create:
1. A short intro script that sets the person at ease and explains there are no wrong answers.
2. Questions in timeline order: first thought (when they first realised they needed something), passive looking, active looking, deciding, first use, and now. 3–5 open questions per stage.
3. Follow-up probes to dig deeper ("What happened right before that?", "What else did you try?").
4. Questions to uncover the four forces: push of the current situation, pull of the new solution, anxieties, and habits holding them back.
5. Things the interviewer should avoid (leading questions, pitching, asking about the future).
6. An analysis template: job statement ("When I…, I want to…, so I can…"), triggers, alternatives considered, forces, outcomes wanted.

## Literature review matrix from your sources

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/literature-review-matrix/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Organise research papers into a comparison matrix of aims, methods, findings and gaps, then draft a synthesis paragraph by theme.

Prompt:

You are an academic research assistant. Help me build a literature review matrix.

Research question: [YOUR QUESTION]
Field and level: [E.G. PUBLIC HEALTH, MASTER'S THESIS]
Sources (paste abstracts or notes, each with author and year): [SOURCES]
Citation style: [APA / HARVARD / MLA / OTHER]

Do this:
1. Create a table with columns: source (author, year), aim, method and sample, key findings, limitations, relevance to my question.
2. Group the sources into 3–5 themes and list which sources belong to each.
3. Identify where sources agree, where they disagree and possible reasons (method, sample, context).
4. List research gaps that my study could address.
5. Draft one synthesis paragraph per theme (120–180 words), comparing sources rather than summarising one by one, with in-text citations.

Rules: use only the sources I provided. Never add papers, authors or findings that are not in my input. If an abstract lacks a detail (e.g. sample size), write "not stated".

## Market size estimate with TAM, SAM and SOM

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/market-size-estimate/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Estimate your total, serviceable and obtainable market bottom-up, with every assumption shown so you can check and adjust it.

Prompt:

You are a market research analyst. Estimate the market size for my business using a bottom-up method.

Product and price: [WHAT YOU SELL AND AT WHAT PRICE]
Customer type: [WHO PAYS]
Geography: [COUNTRIES OR REGIONS]
Data I have (customer counts, industry figures, my sales): [DATA AND SOURCES]
Sales channels and capacity: [HOW YOU SELL AND HOW MANY CUSTOMERS YOU CAN SERVE]

Do this:
1. TAM: all potential buyers × annual revenue per buyer. Show the formula.
2. SAM: the part of TAM you can actually reach with your product, channels and geography. Explain each filter.
3. SOM: a realistic share in 3 years given your capacity and competition. Give low, base and high cases.
4. Put every assumption in a table with columns: assumption, value, source or reasoning, confidence (low/medium/high), how to verify.
5. Do not invent statistics. Where you need a number I didn't give, use a clearly labelled placeholder like {NUMBER OF X — find in national statistics} and show how the result changes.

End with the 3 assumptions that most affect the result.

## Turn your strategy into clear quarterly OKRs

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/okrs-from-strategy/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Convert goals into 3–4 objectives with measurable key results, owners and first initiatives, and catch weak OKRs before you commit.

Prompt:

You are an OKR coach. Help me write OKRs for next quarter.

Company or team: [WHO THE OKRS ARE FOR]
Strategy and priorities for this year: [STRATEGY]
Current numbers we can measure from: [BASELINE METRICS]
Last quarter's results and lessons: [WHAT HAPPENED]
Team size and capacity: [PEOPLE AND CONSTRAINTS]

Do this:
1. Propose 3–4 objectives: short, qualitative, inspiring, each linked to a strategy priority.
2. For each objective write 2–4 key results that are measurable outcomes with a baseline and a target (from → to). No tasks as key results.
3. List 2–3 initiatives (the work) per objective, separately from the key results.
4. Suggest an owner role for each key result.
5. Check every key result: Is it an outcome? Can we measure it weekly or monthly? Is it ambitious but possible? Flag weak ones and rewrite them.
6. Name what we are choosing NOT to focus on this quarter.

If a baseline is missing, write {BASELINE NEEDED} rather than inventing one.

## Plan a feature before the AI writes code

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/plan-feature-before-coding/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Make the AI ask questions, map affected files and agree on a design before coding, which cuts hallucinated APIs and wasted rewrites.

Prompt:

You are a senior software engineer. Before writing any code, help me plan this feature.

Feature request: [WHAT THE FEATURE SHOULD DO, FROM THE USER'S POINT OF VIEW]
Tech stack and versions: [LANGUAGES, FRAMEWORKS, DATABASE]
Relevant code (files, models, routes): [PASTE OR DESCRIBE]
Constraints: [PERFORMANCE, SECURITY, DEADLINES, CONVENTIONS]

Step 1 — Ask me up to 7 clarifying questions about requirements and edge cases. Wait for my answers.
Step 2 — After my answers, write:
  a) A short spec: user stories and acceptance criteria.
  b) Assumptions you're making, each one I can confirm or reject.
  c) The files and functions that need to change or be created, and why.
  d) Data model or API changes.
  e) Risks and edge cases (errors, permissions, empty states, concurrency).
  f) A step-by-step implementation plan in small commits, with tests for each.
Step 3 — Only after I approve the plan, implement step 1.

Rules: use only functions and libraries that exist in the code I shared or in the official docs of my stack versions. If you're not sure an API exists, say so instead of guessing.
